hooks.text: An asteroid zipped 1,830 miles above Earth, yet nobody saw it coming.
How did a car-sized rock sneak past Earth without triggering a warning?
1,830 miles is the distance at which an asteroid surprised the world.

title: The Asteroid That Snuck Past Earth
description: An SUV-sized asteroid passed just 1,830 miles above Earth in 2020, and astronomers were completely blind to it.

beats.text: An asteroid zipped 1,830 miles above Earth, yet nobody saw it coming.
beats.visual: Illustration of a small near-Earth asteroid zooming through space, 2020

beats.text: In August 2020, this SUV-sized space rock approached from the hidden, blinding direction of the bright Sun.
beats.visual: Inner solar system orbit diagram showing Sun and Earth, 2020

beats.text: Traveling at a blistering 27,600 miles per hour, it remained entirely invisible to all our ground-based observatories.
beats.visual: Palomar Observatory Samuel Oschin Telescope dome, 2020

beats.text: Earth's massive gravity then violently bent the trajectory of this rock by roughly 45 degrees of arc.
beats.visual: Diagram of Earth gravity bending an asteroid trajectory, 2020

beats.text: The Zwicky Transient Facility finally spotted the tiny object six hours after its closest, most terrifying approach.
beats.visual: Moving asteroid streak in telescope long exposure image, 2020

beats.text: This event remains the absolute closest non-impacting asteroid flyby ever recorded by our modern global science.
The massive blind spot created by the Sun is why we never saw that asteroid.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of space telescope in orbit, 2020
